summary: Kittitas County lookout: 10-foot timber tower with R-6 cab built 1954, gone by 1988; foundation posts still on the summit, reached by jeep road and trail.

facts.design: 10-foot treated timber tower with R-6 flat-roof cab
facts.status_note: Gone by 1988; sources describe foundation posts or a foundation on the summit and no standing structure

access.note: Reached by a jeep road (Forest Road 3100) and a trail; a gate on the approach may be locked; no source read describes a closure or a permit

visit.trail_note: Willhite: jeep trail climbs 1.2 miles from the Quartz Mountain Road (FR 3100); the final climb is risky. SummitPost (2016): parking by a gate on Forest Road 115, about 3 miles round trip with 500 feet of gain.

events.note: Panoramic photos from the summit dated August 1934 (FFLOS captions them 'Frost Mountain Lookout'; Willhite says panoramics were taken in 1934). See resolved_conflicts.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS captions the August 1934 panoramas 'Frost Mountain Lookout', but the tower is dated 1954 by every source. No source read explains whether an earlier lookout stood there. The story notes the caption and does not reconcile it.
FFLOS says 'gone by 1988' and firelookout.com says 'Gone 1988'; Willhite says 'The lookout lasted 1988.' All three give 1988, so the record uses 1988.

notes_for_editor: Brief record was thin: no height, so height_m 3.0 is added from the 10-foot tower in FFLOS and Willhite (converted, not a stated metre figure). Core dates and design agree across four sources. Staffing and fires: none found in the sources read, so none stated. Today's site is described by Willhite and SummitPost only; neither gives a visit date for the foundation. Visit details are from a 2016 SummitPost note, so check the gate and road before relying on them. The 1934 panorama caption is the one unexplained point.
